scope: Native tile references; graphics retained privately, not a public asset bundle

entries.description: A table scorched with the radial patterns of hot chemistry holds a phial rack and alembic.
Slide drawers of galvanized metal are arranged in a cabinet as rectangles of assorted dimensions. Storage is fractal.
A terracotta board has been painted with ochre and ground iron.
Fabrics were stuffed with watervine chaff and laid across wooden slats in the style of the hillfolk.
A goat wool bed fastened with canvas ties.
Dwellers in the earth-clefts fashion tables in the style of puzzle boxes. Their drawers house the stenographic imagination.
A bridge made of dried brinestalk.
Girthy pilings of fibrous salt-rot stake out these pools of brine. They belong to no one.
Salt-tracing waves cross the grain on the brinestalk pickets stuck into the ground.
Here are several stripped trunks of sallow brinestalk bonded with mud.
Here are several stripped trunks of sallow brinestalk bonded with mud.
Cyclopean blades shaped to the airfoil are housed inside a metallic ring nicked with the scars of time. In the distant past, someone directed the course of air at grand scales.
A jug of aluminum has been sheathed in an olive green cloth for waterkeeping.
Jointed wood and knit watervine make a movable wharf for the ass.
The quickened flax of the earth was duck-weaved in a simple square pattern and hung up on pickets.
Planks of wood are nailed together at right angles in the style of the marsh dwellers.
A wood storage box with a hinged lid and latch. Notches scratched on the surface hint at the full probability array of language, and also its absence.
A tangled nest of roots spill through the earth. The bark is splintered into pointy spines. The leaves are greasy and stinking.
The slate is touched with years of handprints and a ring of rust flakes off the top of the hinges. The door continues, though, its stubborn assertion of 'in' and 'out'.
Wood was precisely cut into drawers and set on brass rails to house clothes.
A cased rotor is fed charge through a handcrank and supplemented by solar heat. Its scratched metal surfaces vibrate at ground frequency.
Stuffed with watervine chaff and glowcrow feathers, this buttoned pillow lets folk repose with crossed legs.

Pieces of the old and aching world have been shaved off their timepoint and crushed to the vicinity of the present. A few bits of recognition remain:  lens of glass, serif of ink, acid-ate lug, and ribbon of wire.
Brinestraw was braided into a rope lattice saddle for slinging between two old oaks and napping. The fibers on the middle-sag are extra frayed from the center-mass strain of a reclining ass.
Wood planks are nailed at orthogonal angles, and dust sleeps on the paper jackets.
A terracotta board has been painted with ochre and ground iron.
A terracotta board has been painted with ochre and ground iron.
Warmth radiates from the crackling fire of the thick clay oven, and with it comes the smell of hot starapple jam and toasted matz.
Handwheel and spindle turn to sand off matter and gift the world with helices and round things. Metal dust accrues on the ground beneath.
Magnetized innards digest electrical signals and belch out the waveform, while a diaphragm breaths dust onto a brass grill.
The biped form emerges out of a cocoon of wood and fiberglass.
Steel was anointed with liquid chrome, cooled, and beaten into a flat and workable surface.
Circles of limestone, porous and oyster-gray with the shells of old things, are arranged in vertical slabs and turned against each other to grind fibrous grains into flours.

Etched chromium on the lavish legs tapers to claw-and-ball feet, and on the marble surface, geometric imperfections were rasped off and flung into an iron bucket that may still exist somewhere. Eaters spoke here, and planned.
Nacreous oil wets the ecru linen and has dripped onto the easel. From the plane of the canvas, an image is pressed out.
A terracotta board has been painted with ochre and ground iron.
A pool of liquid.
Two copper bulbs form a spark gap that facilitates current along a path of ionized gas. The thing snaps and sparks at you.

A vessel of freeblown glass curves at the lunar arc. The style hints that it originates from the coast of the Fuming God Sea, on the far side of Moghra'yi, and that it was likely exported by the dromads.
Sheet metal is locked in diamond pattern and welded to enclose. The surface is scorched and scratched in sections.
A piece of scrap was shed or peeled off a machine fossil.
A piece of scrap was shed or peeled off a machine fossil.
Inside the scratched metal C a needle and a bobbin prepare to punch a pair of threads into a lockstitch. Initials are carved all around its pedestal.
Starapples hang from ashen branches, motes of luscious, red light in a bleached tableau.
Starapples hang from ashen branches, motes of luscious, red light in a bleached tableau.

Branches of the living tree were resorbed and reformed into trunk knots. Then, hundreds of years later, the oiled saw of a gorge woodworker disarranged the arbor geometry and flattened it for civil use. That history remains cast in two dimensions, powdered with dust and scratched in pencil.
A terracotta board has been painted with ochre and ground iron.
A brightly burning handfire hangs across wood and iron.
A large storage vase with a decorative slip. The style hints that it was fired in the home-kiln of a canyon dweller.
Salt gathers in its furrows. It's knotted with moisture-swollen wafers in place of leaves.
A large storage vase with a decorative slip. The style hints that it was fired in the home-kiln of a canyon dweller.
Wood paddles black with wet-rot catch the force of the babbling brook and set the wheel to the slow motion of centuries.
Wood was shaved, cut to smooth-volumed shafts, and fit inside gearboxes to convey motion in continuity.
Marsh reed was handcrossed by warp and weft into a vessel for sheaf and other dry goods.

His mushroom cloud of beard hair is powdered with all the abrasions of the trash sea: white lime, red iron, gold filament, opalescent shavings of the plastiglomerate. Chrome joints and pieces of scrap crystal are hooked to pockets lining his torso, and one of his bushy eyebrows is perpetually cocked, though whether that's a symptom of an insatiable curiosity or forehead mutation is unknown.

Dust powders the puzzling device.

{{K|Weight: 3 lbs.}}

A pair of strapped shoes are cracked on the soles in sinelike patterns of gravel walking.

{{K|Weight: 1 lbs.}}

A warm smile spreads over an old face freckled by time and a million crumbs of salt. He shrinks under a hunched back and drums the ground beneath him with a short and barb-crowned tail. A second pair of arms rise over the slump of his shoulders, where hands meet and fingers lace to form another face, this one vacant and prehistoric, no mouth and eyes desert-white.
{{C|-----}}
Loved by {{C|the villagers of Joppa}}.

Hated by {{C|the villagers of Kiggashur}} for questioning the origins of the moon.

Disliked by {{C|goatfolk}} for casting doubt on their beliefs.

Admired by {{C|the Daughters of Exile}} for respecting the sanctity of a burial site.

Wool was dyed in a bath of dreadroot and iron salt, and then woven to warm broad shoulders.

{{K|Weight: 1 lbs.}}

Two almonds of glass sit in wireframe cups and resharpen the world's edges.

{{K|Weight: 1 lbs.}}

Luminescent flecks flit beneath the water's surface.

Base demeanor: {{g|docile}}

Her kufiya has been cut and resewn to a cowl, and she has tailored a vinewafer sack to approximate the slate habit of the chromaic people. A sheaf of watervine bundled in copper wire is slung on her hip, and she rubs a salt-nailed thumb over a talisman of cracked circuitboard.

Particulate from the eons-sheared shale sticks in the fibers of goat wool. They make red freckles on the garment.

{{K|Weight: 5 lbs.}}

The crown is crushed by wear into a hundred papery creases, and the brim is stained in the fractal signatures of sweat and salt.

{{K|Weight: 1 lbs.}}

He is a wind-carved man with the posture of a vinereaper; his spine is bent to point the bright turquoise of his eyes at the tilling angle, his hips are pushed odd-forward with the slumping ease of a stance much more relaxed than his. If it weren't for the salt on his brow and the scarred knuckles, he would seem a marble Saad perched under a crumbling tomb.
{{C|-----}}
Loved by {{C|the villagers of Joppa}}.

Disliked by {{C|the Seekers of the Sightless Way}} for leading a raiding party on one of their camps.

Disliked by {{C|mysterious strangers}} for torching one of their villages.

A coarse flax waist is cinched with a watervine hemp rope.

{{K|Weight: 5 lbs.}}

Sharp jade eyes are crow-worn to late middle age and her lips are scarred with gas burns. Climbing over her back and neck are the jeweled segments of a great spiral tail and stinger; a bead of smoking gut juice gleams on the tip.

A phosphorescent opal-like fits in the palm of a hand and glows with the light of auroras absorbed chiliads ago. It floats about preternaturally.

{{K|Weight: 0 lbs.}}

Shot ink decorates the dulla on his long neck in one of the thousand patterns of the camelfolk. His ears are arrayed with gilded rings, and eyelashes flow down his face like watervine fronds. Across his back, a hump of moistured and healthy fat pushes his center of mass skyward.

{{K|Weight: 5 lbs.}}

Big Yrame shifts her weight between hind and forelegs. She shakes a storm of rust dander from the tines of her great horns, and she blows a halo of freezing air from her rime-veined hands.
{{C|-----}}
Loved by {{C|the Fellowship of Wardens}}.

Admired by {{C|the villagers of Joppa}} for defending their village.

Disliked by {{C|the villagers of Tuwan}} for disparaging a famous poet.

Disliked by {{C|trees}} for eating one of their young.

A shiny mesh of linked loops that were sourced from the steel heart of the trash sea.

The tatters of a sweat-stained kufiya thrash in the wind from where they hang about the farmer's neck. Clasped in his gnarled, brown hand is a curved vinereaper of iron with which he culls moisture-swollen wafers from the viridian plant called watervine.
